topics.justification: Dominated by "byte", "padding/pad", "length", "block_size", and "multiple", indicating questions about padding schemes, aligning data to block boundaries, and adding/removing padding during encryption.
Strong weights for "key", "iv", "password", "hash", "salt", and "derive/generate" point to deriving encryption keys from passwords and creating/storing random IVs safely.

topics.topic_name: Choosing crypto modes and secure implementations
topics.justification: Words like "mode", "implementation", "library", "security", and "design" suggest conceptual guidance on selecting block cipher modes and implementing them correctly using libraries.

topics.topic_name: Cryptographic security model and attack reasoning
topics.justification: "attack", "adversary/attacker", "scheme", "assume", and "break" indicate theory-focused discussions about what security means (threat models) and how encryption schemes can be attacked or proven secure.
High weights for "code", "file", "encrypt/decrypt", "error", "wrong", and "openssl" match troubleshooting implementation bugs, API misuse, and mismatched parameters in real code.
"block", "mode", "nonce", "stream", and "counter" strongly suggest counter-mode/streaming encryption questions, including nonce/IV sizing and reuse constraints.

topics.topic_name: Plaintext vs ciphertext properties (incl. one-time pad)
topics.justification: Frequent "plaintext", "ciphertext", "time_pad", "random", and "length" indicate discussions about relationships between plaintext/ciphertext, leakage (e.g., length/structure), and comparisons to or misconceptions about one-time pads.
Top words "message", "authentication", "tag", "integrity", "hmac", and "protocol" point to encrypt-then-MAC/AEAD-style designs for sending messages securely with authenticity guarantees.
